tools.name: AddComment
tools.description:
Add a comment or internal work note to a work record.

The note is normally attributed to the authenticated ServiceNow user. Some
instances have a business rule that attributes every journal entry to a
fixed integration/service persona regardless of which OAuth identity made
the write — a structural property of that instance's configuration, not a
per-call fluke. When that happens here, ``warnings`` names the mismatched
author so the discrepancy is visible on every affected write, not just
guessed at afterward. Work notes are internal and visible only to
fulfillers; customer-visible comments are seen by the requestor who opened
the record.

parameters.name: identifier
parameters.description: The record's human-facing number or sys_id.

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: The text of the note to add. Cannot be empty.

parameters.name: audience
parameters.description: Whether this note is internal-only (visible only to fulfillers) or visible to the requestor. Defaults to internal.

parameters.name: record_type
parameters.description: The record's type. Required when identifier is a sys_id; inferred automatically from the number prefix when identifier is a number.

output.description: The record's full details, including the new note in its history.

comment.value: Investigated the issue and found that the root cause is a misconfigured network policy. Updating the firewall rules to resolve the connectivity problem.

tools.name: CreateIncident
tools.description:
Open a new incident. Returns the incident number the caller can quote.

The authenticated ServiceNow user is recorded as the caller unless overridden
with ``caller``. A short description is required; every other field is optional.

parameters.name: short_description
parameters.description: One-line summary of the incident. Cannot be empty.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Detailed description of the incident. Leave empty to omit.

parameters.name: urgency
parameters.description: How quickly this needs to be resolved: 'high', 'medium', or 'low'. Leave empty to use the instance's default.

parameters.name: impact
parameters.description: Business impact: 'high', 'medium', or 'low'. Leave empty to use the instance's default.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Incident category, e.g. 'network', 'hardware', 'software', 'database'. Leave empty to use the instance's default.

parameters.name: caller
parameters.description: Person this incident is being reported for, by email or name. Resolved to a ServiceNow user before creation; an unresolvable or ambiguous match is left unresolved (the incident is still created, attributed to the authenticated caller, and the failure is explained in warnings) rather than blocking creation. Omitting this or leaving it blank attributes the incident to the authenticated caller.

output.description: The newly created incident, including its number.

short_description.value: VPN connection dropping intermittently for remote users

Read a configuration item together with what it depends on and what depends on it.

tools.name: GetRecord
tools.description:
Read a work record together with its full comment and work-note history.

A missing or unreadable identifier returns a not-found envelope (``found``
false) rather than raising, so a stale or guessed identifier can be recovered
within the same turn. When the most recent activity entry's author doesn't
match the authenticated caller, that's reported in ``warnings`` too — some
instances attribute every journal entry to a fixed persona regardless of who
wrote it, so ``author`` in the activity history may not name the true writer.

parameters.name: identifier
parameters.description: The record's human-facing number (e.g. 'INC0010023') or sys_id.

parameters.name: record_type
parameters.description: The record's type. Required when identifier is a sys_id; inferred automatically from the number prefix (INC, PRB, CHG, REQ, RITM, TASK) when identifier is a number.

output.description: The record's full details and activity history, or a not-found envelope.

tools.name: GetRecordCounts
tools.description:
Count work records matching a filter, optionally broken down by a field.

The count reflects only work records the authenticated caller can see —
the same visibility every other tool in this toolkit applies. For
sc_request/sc_req_item, text also matches the ordered catalog item's name,
since a request's own short description is otherwise structurally blank.

parameters.name: record_type
parameters.description: The work-record type to count.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Only count records whose short description contains this text. For sc_request/sc_req_item, also matches the ordered catalog item's name. Leave empty for no text filter.

parameters.name: assigned_to_me
parameters.description: Only count records assigned to the authenticated caller. Defaults to false.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only count records in this state: 'new', 'in_progress', 'on_hold', 'resolved', 'closed', or 'cancelled'. Leave empty for no state filter.

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: Only count records at this priority: 'critical', 'high', 'moderate', 'low', or 'planning'. Leave empty for no priority filter.

parameters.name: active_only
parameters.description: Exclude resolved, closed, and cancelled records. Defaults to true.

parameters.name: opened_after
parameters.description: Only count records opened on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Leave empty for no lower bound.

parameters.name: group_by
parameters.description: A field to break the count down by, e.g. 'priority' or 'assignment_group'. Leave empty for a single total with no breakdown.

output.description: The total count for the filtered set, and a breakdown by group_by if given.

tools.name: GetRecordFieldChoices
tools.description:
Discover the valid choice values for a work-record field on this instance.

Choice lists are instance-customized, so a state or priority filter that
another tool rejected can be corrected by reading the values this returns.

parameters.name: record_type
parameters.description: The work-record type the field belongs to.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The field name to discover valid choices for, e.g. 'state' or 'priority'.

output.description: The instance's valid label/value pairs for that field. When the instance's configured choice list itself isn't readable, this falls back to the values currently in use on existing records, which may omit a configured value no record currently holds. ``available`` is false only when neither source can produce any values, in which case ``choices`` is empty rather than incomplete.

tools.description:
Order an item from the service catalog. Returns the request number.

Every variable marked mandatory on the item must be present in ``variables``,

tools.name: UpdateRecord
tools.description:
Change one or more fields on a work record. Fields not specified are left untouched.

A person or team named by ``assigned_to``/``assignment_group``/``caller`` is resolved
to a real ServiceNow record before anything is written; if the name can't be
resolved (no match, or more than one candidate), that field alone is left
unchanged and explained in ``warnings`` rather than raising, while every other
field given in the same call is still written — so it can be retried with just
the corrected name. A field the instance's own business rules recalculate
or reject after the write (e.g.
``priority`` recomputed from ``impact``/``urgency``, or an invalid ``state``)
is also reported in ``warnings`` when the written value didn't stick. A write
the instance's ACLs reject outright (e.g. a 403 tied to the record's current
assignment) is reported in ``warnings`` the same way, instead of raising.
Changing ``state`` away from a resolved/closed state (reopening a record)
without also setting ``close_code``/``close_notes`` in the same call can
clear those fields as a platform side effect; when that happens it is
reported in ``warnings`` too, not left for a separate read to discover.
When more than one field is given and the instance rejects the combined
write atomically (some business rules abort on a specific field
combination), each field is retried on its own so the ones that apply
cleanly still get written instead of the whole call failing silently.

parameters.name: identifier
parameters.description: The record's human-facing number or sys_id.

parameters.name: record_type
parameters.description: The record's type. Required when identifier is a sys_id; inferred automatically from the number prefix when identifier is a number.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: New state: 'new', 'in_progress', 'on_hold', 'resolved', 'closed', or 'cancelled', or an instance-specific value. Omitting this leaves the existing state unchanged.

parameters.name: assigned_to
parameters.description: Person to assign this record to, by email or name. Resolved to a ServiceNow user before the write; an unresolvable or ambiguous name is reported and nothing is written. Omitting this leaves the existing assignee unchanged.

parameters.name: assignment_group
parameters.description: Team to assign this record to, by name. Resolved to a ServiceNow group before the write, with the same unresolvable/ambiguous handling as assigned_to. Omitting this leaves the existing group unchanged.

parameters.name: caller
parameters.description: Person this record is reported for, by email or name. Resolved to a ServiceNow user before the write, with the same unresolvable/ambiguous handling as assigned_to. Some instances require this to be set before a record can transition to a resolved or closed state. Omitting this leaves the existing caller unchanged.

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: New priority: 'critical', 'high', 'moderate', 'low', or 'planning'. Omitting this leaves the existing priority unchanged.

parameters.name: urgency
parameters.description: New urgency: 'high', 'medium', or 'low'. Omitting this leaves it unchanged.

parameters.name: impact
parameters.description: New impact: 'high', 'medium', or 'low'. Omitting this leaves it unchanged.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: New category, e.g. 'network', 'hardware', 'software', 'database'. Instance-specific value — an invalid value is flagged in warnings with the live list of valid options for this field. Omitting this leaves the existing category unchanged.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Replacement text for the record's detailed description. Omitting this leaves the existing description unchanged.

parameters.name: close_code
parameters.description: Resolution code. Some instances require this when resolving or closing a record. Omitting this leaves it unchanged.

parameters.name: close_notes
parameters.description: Resolution notes describing how the record was resolved. Some instances require this when resolving or closing a record. Omitting this leaves it unchanged.

description.value: User is unable to connect to the VPN. Issue started after the latest system update was applied on Monday morning.

close_notes.value: Rolled back the latest network driver update and restored VPN connectivity. Issue confirmed resolved by the end user.

summary:
ServiceNow toolkit for Arcade enables LLM agents to interact with a ServiceNow ITSM instance — reading, searching, creating, and updating work records, catalog items, knowledge articles, configuration items, and user/group data.

## Capabilities

- **Incident & work record lifecycle**: Open incidents, read full records with activity history, update arbitrary fields (with per-field retry and warnings on ACL rejections or business-rule overrides), add comments or internal work notes, count and search records by text, state, priority, assignment, or recency.
- **Service catalog**: Search catalog items, read item details and mandatory variables, and place orders with pre-submission validation of required and constrained variables.
- **Knowledge base**: Search articles and read full article bodies; access is scoped to what the authenticated caller is entitled to read.
- **CMDB & configuration items**: Search configuration items by name or CMDB class, and read individual CI details including dependency relationships.
- **User, group & field discovery**: Look up users by name or email, find assignment groups by name, and retrieve instance-specific valid choice values for any work-record field.
- **Auth verification**: Confirm the authenticated identity and retrieve the caller's `sys_id` via `WhoAmI` for self-referential filters.

## OAuth

This toolkit uses OAuth 2.0 to authenticate with ServiceNow. Refer to the Arcade auth provider docs for configuration details: [https://docs.arcade.dev/en/references/auth-providers/unknown](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/references/auth-providers/unknown).

## Secrets

- **`SERVICENOW_INSTANCE_URL`**: The base URL of your ServiceNow instance (e.g., `https://yourcompany.service-now.com`). This is not a generated API key — it is simply the root URL of the specific ServiceNow tenant the toolkit should target. You can find it in your browser's address bar when logged into your ServiceNow instance, or by asking your ServiceNow administrator. Every API call is routed to this URL, so it must point to the correct instance (dev, staging, or production). Set this value via the Arcade secrets system.

See the Arcade secrets documentation for how to store and reference secrets: [https://docs.arcade.dev/en/guides/create-tools/tool-basics/create-tool-secrets](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/guides/create-tools/tool-basics/create-tool-secrets). You can also manage secrets directly at [https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/auth/secrets](https://api.arcade.dev/dashboard/auth/secrets).
